correctness.rationale: Exchangeability of sample pairs gives the finite-census index as the expectation. Conditioning on absence of species i, when feasible, gives the same pair probability in the complement census. Cov(I_i,G) is the absence probability times the unconditional-minus-complement index; infeasible terms are zero without defining a conditional expectation. Cancelling the first two factors of the complement falling factorial yields (1). Expansion of the numerator into N(t-1)(N-t)+B(t-a_i), and symmetrization with weights a_i, gives exactly (2); each pair contribution is nonnegative because feasibility-thresholded w_i is nonincreasing in a_i, including at m=2. The first term is strictly positive exactly when 1<t<N and some species can be absent. In all other cases richness or both statistics are constant. Equal abundances annul the correction and attain the lower bound, including nondegenerate positive cases. Independent exact labeled-subset calculation agreed on 2,375 profile/depth pairs, with 1,891 positive and 484 zero.
residual_risks: Exhaustion in the replay is through N=12 only. The theorem is for uniform fixed-size subsets of labeled individuals, not nonuniform or spatial sampling or the empirical with-replacement normalization.

evidence: The Rao record proves nonnegative covariance for arbitrary distances at N<=4 and m=2 (and zero at m=N), and derives its general-distance next-to-census formula for one doubleton plus singletons. Colwell and Nipperess–Matsen give hypergeometric rarefaction and presence-indicator machinery for richness/phylogenetic-diversity moments.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Credit the overlapping sign cases and next-to-census subfamily. Broader dissimilarity scope there is paired with narrower abundance or depth scope; the fixed-distance all-population sign is not a specialization of the theorem as a whole. Branch-indicator covariances alone do not supply a mixed richness–pair-diversity sign law.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The iid formulation is not equivalent: even with probabilities a_i/N, pair and absence laws differ and census saturation need not occur under iid draws. The Rao observable shares exactly the equal-distance specialization, but its covered abundance/depth ranges do not cover this universal specialization. Its negative witness uses unequal distances and is no contradiction.

October 4 iid result and October 18 unequal-distance Rao witness
value.rationale: The result gives an exact dependent-sampling law for two widely used rarefaction summaries. Its sign, attained bound and exact zero threshold give information not available from the two marginal means or an iid calculation; in particular, the loss of covariance as richness saturates is characterized for arbitrary abundance profiles. The Rao comparison shows the equal-distance scope is a real mathematical boundary, not a normalization convention.
residual_risks: The result does not imply ecological causation, positive association for other statistics, or a sign guarantee for unequal pairwise dissimilarities.
